cases.sentence: Ну вот, я же знал, что говорил: пойдешь направо – обязательно попадешь на ___.
cases.explain: «Курский вокзал» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: There you are. I did know what I was talking about. You turn right and inevitably you get to the Kursk Station. You were bored there in the back alleys, Venichka, and you wanted to rub elbows with the crowd, so there you are.

cases.sentence: Ведь в человеке не одна только физическая сторона; в нем и ___ есть, и есть – больше того – есть сторона мистическая, сверхдуховная сторона.
cases.explain: «духовная сторона» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: I walked across the square. Rather, I was drawn across it. I stopped two or three times and froze on the spot in order to get the queasiness under control. Because, after all, a person has more than just a physical side. He has a spiritual side as well and, more than that, there’s a mystical, a superspiritual side. So, there I was in the square expecting any minute to get sick on all three sides. And, again, I’d stop and freeze.

cases.sentence: Да сверхчеловек и свалился бы после ___ охотничьей, так и не выпив второго…
cases.explain: «первого стакана» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "So, when was it you bought your goodies yesterday? After the Hunter’s? No, after the Hunter’s I wasn’t up to buying presents. Between the first and second glass of Hunter's? No, between the two glasses there was a break of thirty seconds, and I’m not superhuman and able to get something done in thirty seconds. Anyway, a superhuman being would have collapsed after the first glass of Hunter's and never made it to the second. So when was it? By the grace of God, how many mysteries there are in the world! An impenetrable veil of mysteries. Before the Coriander or between the beer and the Albe de dessert?"’
